questions.q: What is catastrophic forgetting, structurally, in the context of fine-tuning a language model?
options: A bug specific to one particular training framework

The tendency of gradient descent, which has no explicit mechanism protecting previously learned capabilities, to overwrite weight configurations that encoded performance on earlier tasks while fitting a new, narrower task
A hardware failure that corrupts model checkpoints
A property that only affects models larger than 100 billion parameters
questions.explain: Catastrophic forgetting is a structural consequence of how gradient descent works: it only minimizes loss on the current data, with no built-in protection for capabilities learned on previous, different data.

questions.q: Why can catastrophic forgetting go completely unnoticed by a team fine-tuning a model?
options: Because it only happens during pretraining, never during fine-tuning
Because if only the target fine-tuning task is evaluated after training, a team can see the task metric improve while missing a simultaneous regression in general-capability benchmarks never measured
Because catastrophic forgetting always shows up as a training crash
Because it is impossible to measure under any circumstances
questions.explain: The failure pattern is specific: task-specific metrics improve while general-capability benchmarks regress. Teams that evaluate only on the target task can miss this regression entirely.

questions.q: Which combination of conditions tends to increase the risk of catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning?
options: A low learning rate, few epochs, and a broad, diverse dataset
A high learning rate, many epochs over a small dataset, and a training set narrow in topic relative to the model's original distribution
Using a larger batch size with no other changes
Switching from fp16 to bf16 precision
questions.explain: Higher learning rates produce larger per-step overwrites, more epochs mean repeated exposure to a narrow distribution, and a topically narrow dataset lacks the diversity to counterbalance forgetting -- all three compound the risk.

questions.q: How do parameter-efficient methods like LoRA provide a structural mitigation against catastrophic forgetting, beyond their memory savings?
options: They increase the learning rate automatically to prevent forgetting
Because the base model's weights stay frozen and untouched, the pretrained knowledge encoded in them is mechanically protected from being overwritten; only the small adapter is fit to the new task
They eliminate the need for any evaluation after fine-tuning
They guarantee zero forgetting under all conditions
questions.explain: Since LoRA freezes the base weights entirely, the pretrained knowledge they encode cannot be directly overwritten, reducing (though not eliminating) the risk of catastrophic forgetting compared to full fine-tuning.

questions.q: What practical evaluation discipline does this lesson recommend to detect catastrophic forgetting?
options: Evaluate only on the fine-tuning target task, since that is the only metric that matters
Evaluate the fine-tuned model on a general-capability benchmark suite in addition to the target task, comparing against the pre-fine-tuning checkpoint
Skip evaluation entirely and trust the training loss curve alone
Only evaluate forgetting after deploying the model to production users
questions.explain: The recommended discipline is to evaluate general capability alongside the target task, comparing against the pre-fine-tuning checkpoint, so any regression is visible and the trade-off is made deliberately rather than discovered later.
